# HUD NSPIRE FULL REGULATORY TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION & COMPLIANCE BLUEPRINT

## Standard Authority: Title 24 CFR Part 5 Subpart G
Federal Register Reference: 88 FR 30442 & 88 FR 43382
Program Coverage: Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher (HCV), Project-Based Vouchers (PBV), Public Housing, Section 8 Multifamily, CPD, Section 202/811.

---

## 1. Statutory Architecture & Transition from UPCS/HQS to NSPIRE
On October 1, 2023, the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) formally sunsetted the Uniform Physical Condition Standards (UPCS) and Housing Quality Standards (HQS), establishing the National Standards for the Physical Inspection of Real Estate (NSPIRE).

Key structural changes under NSPIRE:
1. Re-prioritization of the Resident Unit: Under UPCS, exterior aesthetic defects (such as hairline sidewalk cracks or chipped paint on dumpster enclosures) could sink an inspection score while internal residential hazards went under-weighted. Under NSPIRE, over 50% of the total score is derived from conditions inside the tenant's dwelling unit.
2. Binary Defect Categorization: Every observed deficiency is explicitly defined with objective metrics (e.g., crack width, distance in inches, temperature range in degrees Fahrenheit) to reduce inspector subjectivity.
3. Affirmative Life-Threatening (LT) Citations: A single Life-Threatening defect triggers a mandatory 24-hour cure notice. Failure to upload photo proof of remediation within 24 hours into HUD's electronic portal causes immediate abatement of subsidy disbursements.

---

## 2. Definitive Defect Classifications & Remediation Timelines

### Tier 1: Life-Threatening (LT)
- Remediation Window: Mandatory 24 hours from time of inspection.
- Enforcement: Failure results in immediate voucher payment abatement or referral to HUD Enforcement Center.
- Core Items:
  * Inoperable or missing smoke alarm in bedroom, hallway, or any level.
  * Smoke alarm with removable 9V batteries (sealed 10-year lithium required on battery-only units).
  * Missing carbon monoxide detector in units with fuel-burning appliances or attached garages.
  * Absence of ground-fault circuit-interrupter (GFCI) protection within 6 feet of sinks/water sources.
  * Missing, plugged, or incorrectly sized water heater Temperature and Pressure Relief (TPR) valve discharge pipe (must terminate 2" to 6" from the floor).
  * Obstructed or unopenable primary bedroom emergency egress window.
  * Double-cylinder deadbolts requiring key to exit from the interior.
  * Exposed live electrical conductors, missing faceplates, or open panel knockout holes.
  * Detected natural gas, propane, or methane leaks.
  * Blocked primary or secondary fire egress pathways.

### Tier 2: Severe Deficiencies
- Remediation Window: 24 hours or 30 days depending on specific HUD program schedule.
- Core Items:
  * Inoperable primary heating system during cold weather periods (ambient indoor temp below 68°F).
  * Water supply absent or non-functional; hot water temperature below 100°F or exceeding 120°F.
  * Sewage backup into living units or common spaces.
  * Structural stability concerns in foundation, load-bearing walls, or ceiling assemblies.

### Tier 3: Moderate & Low Deficiencies
- Remediation Window: 30 to 60 calendar days.
- Core Items:
  * Minor moisture staining or plumbing leaks under sinks without active pooling.
  * Damaged interior door latches, missing strikes, or damaged cabinet doors.
  * Minor peeling paint in non-child occupied post-1978 properties.
  * Minor exterior site grading issues or gutter downspout misalignments.

---

## 3. Comprehensive Room-by-Room Inspection Audit Protocol

### Unit Living Area & Bedrooms
- [ ] Smoke alarms installed and operational on ceiling or upper 12" of wall.
- [ ] Egress window opens fully without tools and stays elevated without props.
- [ ] All electrical outlets tested for open ground, reverse polarity, and cracked casing.
- [ ] Closet light fixtures have approved safety covers (no bare incandescent bulbs near combustible materials).
- [ ] Minimum 2 working electrical receptacles per habitable room or 1 receptacle and 1 permanent light fixture.

### Kitchen Areas
- [ ] Every outlet within 6 feet of sink basin has functioning GFCI trip protection.
- [ ] Range burners ignite promptly without gas pooling or manual match requirement.
- [ ] Range anti-tip bracket installed at base of stove to prevent tipping during door loading.
- [ ] Range hood or kitchen exhaust fan operational.
- [ ] Sink plumbing free of active leaks, corrosion, or slow drainage.

### Bathroom Facilities
- [ ] GFCI protection installed and verified functional within 6 feet of basin.
- [ ] Mechanical exhaust ventilation fan operational or window with screen that opens.
- [ ] Hot water delivery verified between 100°F and 120°F.
- [ ] Toilet securely bolted to floor flange without rocking; flush mechanism functions properly.
- [ ] Tub/shower surround sealed with clean, mildew-free caulking to prevent water infiltration.

### Mechanical & Utility Systems
- [ ] Water heater TPR safety valve equipped with rigid metal (copper) or CPVC discharge pipe terminating 2"-6" above floor.
- [ ] Electrical breaker panel door closes fully; all knockout openings sealed with UL-listed plugs; zero open slots without circuit breakers or blanks.
- [ ] Clothes dryer exhaust duct constructed of rigid metal ducting venting directly to outdoors (flexible foil/vinyl ducting prohibited).
- [ ] HVAC air filter installed; condensate drain line unobstructed.

### Exterior Grounds & Common Areas
- [ ] Stairways with 4 or more risers equipped with secure handrails (34" to 38" height).
- [ ] Porches, balconies, or walking surfaces 30" or higher above grade equipped with 36"+ guardrails with baluster spacing under 4".
- [ ] Exterior lighting operational above all common entrance doorways.
- [ ] Garbage disposal facilities adequate with secure rodent-proof lids.
- [ ] Address numbers clearly visible from the street curb (minimum 4" reflective font).

---

## 4. Official Technical Appeal & Scoring Dispute Framework (45-Day Rule)
Under HUD 24 CFR § 5.711, property owners possess the right to file an administrative request for technical review within 45 calendar days of receiving the official REAC inspection report.

Valid grounds for technical appeal:
1. Significant Objective Error: The inspector cited a standard that does not apply to the specific property type or recorded an incorrect deficiency category.
2. Tenant Responsibility: The defect was caused directly by tenant refusal or prohibited alteration with documented contemporaneous landlord cure notices.
3. Pre-Approved Waivers or Approved Modernization Work-in-Progress: Active capital improvement projects under approved housing authority contracts prior to the inspection notice date.

Documentation required for appeal:
- Signed Technical Review Request letter citing specific 24 CFR § 5.711 criteria.
- Contemporaneous high-resolution dated photographic evidence.
- Licensed contractor diagnostic work orders and local building department code interpretations.
